concepts.title: Circle and ring areas
concepts.explanation: A circle has area πr². An annular ring has area π(R² − r²), the difference of two circle areas. Use the stated value of π.

example.problem: A circular plate has diameter 28 cm. Find its area in cm². Use π = 22/7.

concepts.commonMistake: Doubling radius multiplies area by four, not two.
checklist: Convert diameter to radius if needed.

concepts.title: Sector area
concepts.explanation: A sector with central angle θ° has area (θ/360)πr². The angle fraction describes the fraction of the full circle.

example.problem: Find the area of a 120° sector of radius 14 cm in cm². Use π = 22/7.
steps: The sector is one third of the circle: area = 616/3.

checklist: Find the fraction of a full turn.
Multiply full area by that fraction.

concepts.title: Arc length
concepts.explanation: Arc length for central angle θ° is (θ/360)2πr. It is a curved length, measured in linear units.

example.problem: Find the length in cm of a 60° arc of radius 14 cm. Use π = 22/7.

concepts.commonMistake: The sector area formula uses r²; arc length uses r.

concepts.title: Sector perimeter
concepts.explanation: A sector perimeter is its arc plus two radii. A semicircle’s perimeter is πr + 2r. Boundaries shared inside a composite shape are not exposed perimeter.

example.problem: Find the perimeter in cm of a 90° sector of radius 14 cm. Use π = 22/7.
steps: The arc is 22; add two radii 28.

concepts.commonMistake: Arc length alone omits the straight boundary pieces.
checklist: Add the arc and straight pieces.

concepts.title: Minor segment area
concepts.explanation: A minor segment is the region between a chord and its minor arc. Its area equals minor-sector area minus the area of the triangle formed by the two radii.

example.problem: A chord subtends 90° at the centre of a radius-14 cm circle. Find the minor segment area in cm². Use π = 22/7.
steps: Sector = 154. The right triangle has area r²/2 = 98.

concepts.commonMistake: Subtract triangle area from sector area, not from the full circle.
